data.title: KKR in talks to buy majority stake in EdgeCore - report
data.description:
KKR & Co. (KKR) unit Helix Digital Infrastructure is in talks to acquire a majority stake in EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The operator of high-density, hyperscale data centers built for cloud and AI workloads could be valued between $8B and $10B, according to one of the sources.

Helix is expected to buy the stake from Partners Group Holding, said the people, asking not to be identified because the information is confidential.

data.title: Fed shouldn’t hike again after December – OnePoint BFG Wealth’s Peter Boockvar
data.description:
The Federal Reserve should not raise interest rates again after December, said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer of OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners.

He cited turmoil in the AI tech trade, declining industrial metals prices, and falling crude oil prices (CL1:COM).

"I just don't see how the Fed will hike again after December, if they even do then, if this selloff and AI CapEx concerns continue," he said.

The investment strategist pointed to the outsized role that artificial intelligence plays in the current economy as the reason for the Fed to exercise caution. Data center construction accounts for roughly half of GDP growth, AI-related companies represent approximately half of the S&P 500's (SP500) market capitalization, and the sector drives about 75% of earnings growth.

He noted that upper-income consumers are heavily dependent on the wealth effect from a stock market largely propelled by the AI trade.

"If the economic contribution from the data center build wasn't about half of GDP growth, if it wasn't about half the S&P 500 in terms of market cap, if it wasn't about 75% of earnings growth right now, and if the upper-income U.S. consumer wasn't so dependent on the wealth effect of a higher stock market mostly being driven by the AI trade, I'd say the Fed can look past this all with their inflation focus, but that's not where we stand," Boockvar explained.

While he expressed confidence that Kevin Warsh is monitoring these developments, he suggested some Fed colleagues "aren't reading the full room."

Peter Tchir, head of Macro Strategy at Academy Securities, echoed similar concerns about monetary policy tightening.

"They should probably avoid hiking in December too," he said, reinforcing the broader skepticism among market strategists about near-term rate increases.

data.title: Playboy to exit Russell 3000 in December reconstitution
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of additions and deletions to its Russell 3000 index. The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the US markets close on December 11.

The Russell 3000 Index tracks the performance of the 3,000 largest U.S. companies and is designed to represent roughly 98% of the investable U.S. equity market.

No consumer staples company will be added to the index during the latest reshuffle, while Playboy (PLBY) is the only stock being deleted.

data.title: North Dakota oil producers moving crude by truck as pipeline outage continues
data.description:
North Dakota oil producers are moving crude by truck as a prolonged outage of Enbridge's (ENB) pipeline in the state forces them to seek alternatives to avoid shutting in production.

"Some producers and marketers are trucking out production to delivery points on the Dakota Access Pipeline," Energy Aspects' head of global crude Jeremy Irwin told Bloomberg in an interview Friday. "Their tanks are filling up, and they can't get enough trucks to evacuate the Bakken crude they have, which could potentially lead to production shut-ins."

The North Dakota Pipeline, which delivers as much as 465K bbl/day of light, sweet crude to Canada and U.S. refineries, has been operating at lower rates since last week after a surge in reports of tainted crude forced Enbridge (ENB) to implement testing for organic chlorides, slowing down the system.

It is unclear when the pipeline will resume normal production, and Energy Aspects said the source of the contamination must be identified and addressed before the system can fully restart.

Demand for Bakken alternatives from Canadian fields is increasing, reportedly prompting Enbridge (ENB) to tell customers it will cut requested light crude shipments at Kerrobert, Saskatchewan, by 24% in December, the highest apportionment since February.

Marathon Petroleum's MPLX midstream arm reportedly issued a force majeure on North Dakota oil pipeline deliveries earlier this week.

data.title: Beyond Meat among consumer staples names set to join Russell Microcap Index
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of additions and deletions to its Russell Microcap Index. The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the U.S. market close on December 11.

The Russell Microcap Index tracks the performance of the micro-cap segment of the U.S. equity market.

The consumer staples companies that are slated to join the index include: Beyond Meat (BYND), B&G Foods (BGS), Healthy Choice Wellness (HOST), Idaho Copper (COPR), SkinHealth Systems (SKIN), and Zone Frontier (ZONE).

The consumer staple names that are leaving the index include: Barfresh Food Group (BRFH), Laird Superfood (LSF), Petmed Express (PETS), and Reeds (REED).

data.title: Bruker a new Sector Perform at RBC as gains 'appear in the rearview'
data.description:
• RBC Capital Markets initiated Bruker (BRKR) at Sector Perform, saying that the life sciences scientific instruments maker is likely past its prime in producing opportunities for gains.
  • The firm has a price target (~6% upside based on Nov. 19 close). 
  • The rating and price target "reflect an appreciation for Bruker's innovation in scientific instruments balanced against the over reliance on semiconductor capital equipment (~10% of sales) for its next cycle of outperformance," analyst Dan Leonard said.
  • He added that upside for the stock is reliant on the semiconductor capital expenditure cycle.
  • "Compared to Life Science Tools peers, Bruker is overexposed to academic/government markets (~35% of sales vs ~10% average), Europe (~37% vs ~30% avg), and instruments (>60% vs 20% avg)," Leonard wrote. "This exposure is mismatched to current growth trends."
  • Bruker shares are down ~7% in Friday afternoon trading.

data.title: Waiting to act when a policy adjustment is required has a cost, says Fed's Cook
data.description:
Waiting to act when a policy adjustment is required has a cost, according to the Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook.

"In my view, financial conditions are too accommodative at a time when inflation remains stubbornly above target, with no clear signs of disinflation in train," she said.

"As a result, holding our policy rate steady will lead to a positive and widening output gap and increasing inflationary pressure. Indeed, we are seeing elevated inflation in a broad swath of goods and services. I see the act of holding the rate steady as much a monetary policy action as the act of increasing the rate."

"Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve. If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households," said Cook.

Cook was speaking on "The U.S. Economy in a Global Context" before the Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Chile.

On the AI buildout, Cook said recent analysis from the International Monetary Fund suggests that advanced economies may be positioned to capture a disproportionate share of global AI-driven productivity growth over the next decade, relative to developing economies.

"AI is likely to cause a shift in the labor market with jobs and job tasks being replaced by AI, and new jobs—many of which we cannot yet conceive of—being created. Ultimately, history has shown that human innovation will likely lead to a successful transition, with permanent job loss unlikely," said the Federal Open Market Committee's voting member.

"In the U.S., labor markets appear resilient to date, but AI adoption is still in its early stages, and I think it is too soon to feel comforted," she said.

"We do see that some workers have already been affected by AI. For instance, there is already some evidence that labor demand has cooled for coding jobs in the software industry and in simultaneous translation. In addition, younger adults are experiencing prolonged job searches, which some attribute to nascent pressure from AI on entry-level positions. As AI adoption spreads, younger workers may continue to be disproportionately affected, and firms may need to take innovative and creative steps to train their future workforce."

"The AI buildout is a global undertaking, and it is reshaping economies—including economies in this region—in ways that are only beginning to be understood," said Cook.

"Over the past two years, the U.S. has raised tariffs on a wide range of imports, and considerable uncertainty remains about where tariff levels will ultimately settle. In the U.S., the effects of tariffs on inflation appear to have moderated, even as uncertainty about future trade policy persists," said Cook.

"China, too, has increased trade restrictions, limiting exports of critical minerals for which it supplies a large fraction of the world's production. These minerals are a crucial input, and uncertainty is rising around the world about access to them," she noted.

"When trade relationships between major economies are altered, other countries must decide how to respond: whether to deepen commercial ties elsewhere, reconfigure supply chains, or wait for greater clarity before committing to new investment," said Cook.

Developing... Check back for updates.

data.title: Trump officials met privately with investors on Norfolk/Union Pacific deal - Bloomberg
data.description:
Trump officials met privately with a group of hedge fund investors who are betting on the outcome of Union Pacific's (UNP) $72 billion acquisition of Norfolk Southern (NSC).

The meeting included investors from several major hedge funds and multiple officials from Trump's administration, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. The funds that attended the meeting specialize in merger arbitrage.

Administration officials didn't share non-public information at the meeting, according to the report.

A White House official said in a statement to Bloomberg that a junior staffer, who no longer works at the White House, attended a lunch off the White House complex and that his attendance wasn’t authorized.

Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) filed a response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City's (CP) request that the Surface Transportation Board terminate review of the merger application for a transcontinental railroad.

The Dept. of Justice is expected to give its opinion on the deal by Dec. 3. The DOJ is likely to remain neutral on the rail combination, according to traders, who cited a Capitol Forum report at the time.

The STB is expected to issue its final decision within 90 days of the record closing, targeting final approval and transaction completion by late summer 2027.

data.title: Wall Street sinks as the tech space remains under heavy pressure
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages were lower on Friday, as a further tech selloff has put the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.7%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -2.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -3.6%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, five of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with consumer staples leading the way higher, while info tech has been the weakest area. 

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's (ANT) much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities. 

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) dropped 12 basis points to 4.65%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) shifted down 10 basis points to 4.94%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) moved down 7 basis points to 5.33%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) advanced +5.2%, while shares of Sandisk (SNDK) dropped -14.4%.

data.title: Nestlé looks to tech giants to automate production -- WSJ
data.description:
Nestlé (NSRGY) is looking to automate its production lines and is working with tech giants to develop AI-powered robots that will be able to run manufacturing and make decisions with little to no human intervention.

“At a certain point in time you can put agentic AI on top of it, and then it’s orchestrating the entire flow. The fully autonomous line is one of the future. We will still need our experts, because we need expert judgment in most cases,” said Nestlé's technology chief Stefan Palzer to The Wall Street Journal.

Nestlé (NSRGY) is working with Microsoft (MSFT) and Boston Dynamics to develop AI and engineering solutions and exploring potential partnerships with Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) and Apple (AAPL).

With the aim to “drive business growth,” Palzer said that these partnerships will enable Nestle’s production lines to fully understand and adapt to variable inputs and produce consistent output.

An increased dependence on automation and artificial intelligence in the food industry comes with unique challenges but will help facilitate operational efficiencies and enable manufacturing to better adapt to changing consumer habits.

“Technology can help with reformulation and product development, but execution will matter more than the tools,” an analyst with Swiss bank Vontobel said to the WSJ.
